Integrate the acceleration: $v=\int(-2t+3)\,dt=-t^2+3t+C$.

The particle is at rest at $t=1$ and $t=2$, so $v=0$ there: $-1+3+C=0\Rightarrow C=-2$. Hence
$$v=-t^2+3t-2=-(t-1)(t-2).$$
Sign of $v$: $v<0$ for $0\le t<1$, $v>0$ for $1<t<2$, $v<0$ for $t>2$.

So the displacement decreases until $t=1$ (local minimum), increases until $t=2$ (local maximum), then decreases for $t>2$. Graph A is the only graph with a minimum at $t=1$, a maximum at $t=2$ and decreasing afterwards. (Graph B has the turning points the wrong way round; C and D do not have stationary points at both $t=1$ and $t=2$.)

**Answer: A**

solutions.check: Checked v=-t^2+3t-2 is zero at t=1,2 and a=dv/dt=-2t+3; matched the sign pattern of v (-,+,-) to the slopes of graph A.
